title: First Unique Character
prompt: A support queue marks each ticket with a short code. Write a function that scans the code from left to right and returns the first character that appears exactly once. If every character repeats, return an empty string.

explanation.beginner:
Example: firstUnique("forge") produces "f". Track the key that defines equality and retain one representative according to the contract’s ordering rule.

Compare “skips repeated leading characters”: input ["swiss"] produces "w". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Track the key that defines equality and retain one representative according to the contract’s ordering rule.

Tempting mistake: Deduplicating objects by reference does not deduplicate equal IDs. Keep duplicate handling and output order explicit.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “skips repeated leading characters”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
